articles.title: Tokyo Opener ‘Sukiyaki’ Director Zeze Takahisa on the Protest Roots of a Global Japanese Pop Hit: ‘The Culture Used to Be Wide Open – Now It’s Become Narrower’
articles.summary: The opening film of the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival, Zeze Takahisa’s “Sukiyaki” tells the story of how the title tune became a worldwide hit in 1963 as well as a beloved standard that has been recorded in foreign-language versions that have also topped charts.
body: Interviewed at the headquarters of Toho, the film’s Japan distributor, Zeze stressed the film’s relevance, six decades after “Sukiyaki,” known locally as “Ue o Muite Aruko” (I’ll Walk with My Head Up”), first hit the charts. “Back then the country was recovering from the war and all sorts of influences were flooding in from abroad,” Zeze said. “Those influences created an energy that propelled the popular culture here. Now Japan is absorbing fewer influences from abroad. The culture used to be wide open – now it’s become narrower.”

But younger Japanese are now discovering that energy from the Showa Era (1926-1989), the period of Emperor Showa’s reign, when Japanese pop culture was at a fertile peak. Together with nostalgic Boomers, they could be found in the audience of “Godzilla Minus One,” the 2023 smash hit Godzilla series installment set in the early postwar period. The follow-up by director Yamazaki Takashi, “Godzilla Minus Zero” is also at TIFF as the festival’s Centerpiece screening, “It’s a kind of Showa boom,” joked Zeze.

articles.title: Tom Skerritt obituary
articles.summary: US actor who often played authority figures and was admired for his film roles in Alien, Top Gun and A River Runs Through It. The lean, rugged US actor Tom Skerritt, who has died aged 93, was described by one screenwriter as “a character actor trapped in a leading man’s body”.
body: Skerritt’s breakthrough had come in the 1970 film M*A*S*H, directed by Robert Altman. He played Augustus “Duke” Forrest, a US army surgeon in the Korean war exuding southern charm at the 4077th Mobile Army Surgical Hospital. Along with his fellow surgeons, Benjamin Franklin “Hawkeye” Pierce ( played by Donald Sutherland ) and “Trapper” John McIntyre (Elliott Gould), Duke displayed cynicism and irreverence towards his superiors.

But Skerritt’s character was not transferred to the TV series that followed. While some sources reported that the actor had no faith in the film working as a half-hour sitcom, the writer Larry Gelbart, who adapted the novel for the small screen with Gene Reynolds, explained they wanted characters they felt could generate storylines, adding: “Trapper John just seemed more colourful than Duke.”

Skerritt remained prolific in character roles in films and on TV until coming to worldwide attention as the doomed Captain Dallas, in charge of the commercial space tug Nostromo, in the sci-fi horror movie Alien (1979), which made a star of Sigourney Weaver.
points: US actor who often played authority figures and was admired for his film roles in Alien, Top Gun and A River Runs Through It.

articles.title: Hasan Piker Sues Scott Jennings for $72 Million Over Out-of-Context Lynching Quote
articles.summary: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker sued conservative commentator Scott Jennings on Tuesday, alleging that Jennings had defamed him by misconstruing a quote to make it sound like Piker endorsed lynchings. On his own podcast on Aug.
body: In the lawsuit, Piker’s attorneys state that it was clear that Piker was mocking another person’s argument — not offering his own support for lynchings — and that Jennings repeatedly contorted Piker’s words to convey the opposite of his actual meaning.

“These were not expressions of disagreement with Mr. Piker’s politics,” the lawsuit states. “Nor were they rhetorical characterizations of an admittedly controversial commentator. They were factual assertions about what Mr. Piker had said and advocated in his work. Each statement was demonstrably false.”

Piker threatened to sue Jennings, who appears frequently on CNN, within a couple of days of the original comments. The controversy has already been adjudicated by Snopes, the myth-busting site, which came down on Piker’s side.

“A full review of Piker’s unedited remarks confirms Jennings falsely claimed Piker said he was in favor of bringing back lynchings,” the site concluded. “In the original stream, Piker’s remarks on lynchings were sarcastic reactions to a user’s chat comment and opinions expressed by someone else in a separate video.”

articles.title: ‘How on earth is this man not sweating?’ Director Brett Morgen’s painstaking 10-year remaser Bowie’s ‘greatest filmed performance’
articles.summary: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgan has turned lost footage of two 1978 concerts into an arena spectacular. ‘You can feel the danger and excitement’, he says. • ‘Lost’ 1978 David Bowie tour film to play arenas in 2027, remastered by Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen.
body: I n 2017, when Brett Morgen began work on his acclaimed 2022 David Bowie documentary, Moonage Daydream, he was given complete access to the late star’s entire, cavernous archive. “My eyes were immediately drawn to a stack of gleaming 35mm cans with the word ‘Stage’ written on them,” he remembers.

At first, the director – whose work also includes Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck and the Rolling Stones documentary Crossfire Hurricane – assumed the cans might contain some sort of footage shot around Bowie’s 1978 live album, Stage, recorded in mostly in Philadelphia. However, he soon realised they actually contained the holy grail of Bowie artefacts: footage of the legendary Earl’s Court shows later that year, which had remained unseen for almost 50 years. “Making Moonage Daydream, I had access to every filmed performance in existence of David Bowie,” he says, “but when I saw this one I knew this was without question the greatest filmed performance of his career.”

articles.title: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
articles.summary: It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t. Think back.
body: Think back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up, Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI. And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

articles.summary: Alex Edelman, Walton Goggins and Connie Britton livened up the A-list fundraiser, which featured powerful speeches from the night's honorees and an impromptu round of applause for Bajaria.
body: Hollywood power players turned out in full force at Saban Community Clinic’s milestone 50th anniversary gala on Monday evening to toast a few of their own inside the Beverly Hills Hotel’s Crystal Ballroom.

A majority came to support the cause (growing more urgent by the day ) and celebrate the night’s headliner honorees, Amazon MGM Studios’ Peter Friedlander and former Showtime chief David Nevins, while others, however, quipped they couldn’t escape the gravitational pull of event linchpin Ellen Hoberman or longtime Saban champions like event chair Richard Weitz. The WME co-chairman was also responsible for one of the night’s heartwarming moments as he led an impromptu and thunderous round of applause for ousted Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria, his fellow event chair, during shared time at the podium at top of the show.

articles.title: Arnie & Barney review – dimwit ant double-act from Maya the Bee are on mission to entertain
articles.summary: From the ugly design to the lacklustre script, this is one parents might want to skip this half-term holiday. In 1912 in Germany, antisemitic writer Waldemar Bonsels published The Adventures of Maya the Bee, which later became a 1970s anime series in Japan called Maya the Honey Bee, and was later…
body: The film opens very much in media res, with a young female bee flying through outer space clutching a small pig and droplet of water the size of her head. She’s being pursued aggressively by a handful of wasp-type creatures and a narrator solemnly intones: “Sometimes the most unlikely heroes … become legends.” The bee then stops next to a couple of red ants and asks what they’re doing. They are the narrators, they explain, but this his is all soon revealed as fantasy – the pair of ants are telling a story to a larger platoon of ants. Some exposition follows about the ants’ mission: to find fresh water.

This is fine as far as it goes, perhaps, but what a précis can’t convey is quite how staggeringly ugly and uninteresting the whole endeavour is. It starts with the character design: it’s hard to imagine any but the most aesthetically starved children embracing this ant pair. Boy are they a chore to spend time with, both visually and in terms of the lacklustre script. Even if you are struggling for entertainment options you might want to do the kids a favour and skip this one.
points: From the ugly design to the lacklustre script, this is one parents might want to skip this half-term holiday.

articles.title: VisionQuest Finally Explains The Biggest Plot Hole From Avengers: Age Of Ultron
articles.summary: Avengers: Age of Ultron didn't exactly flesh out Ultron's motivations for doing what he does. Now, VisionQuest Episode 5 is finally correcting that.
body: In so doing, "VisionQuest" retroactively addresses one of the biggest complaints about "Age of Ultron" — namely, Ultron's rather rushed motivations — and makes the film even better.

Remember all those memes about Ultron needing only 10 seconds on the internet in order to decide that humanity collectively needed to be wiped out? As funny as they were, those jokes also pointed to one of the more obvious shortcomings in "Avengers: Age of Ultron." For an ambitious sequel that already had so much going on, there wasn't exactly much screen time devoted to the "why" behind Ultron's murderous intent. Sure, James Spader made an absolute meal out of his speeches about puppets on strings and evolution and "peace in our time." But, when it comes down to it, could audiences really grasp the underlying reason(s) why Ultron became so bad in the first place?
points: Avengers: Age of Ultron didn't exactly flesh out Ultron's motivations for doing what he does.
Now, VisionQuest Episode 5 is finally correcting that.
